meta.title: AirDrop Alternative That Works on Every Device | BIShare
meta.description: Need an AirDrop alternative that isn’t Apple-only? BIShare sends files across iPhone, Android, Windows, Mac and Linux — nearby or by browser link. Free, no account.

hero.title: The AirDrop alternative for every device
hero.body: AirDrop only speaks to Apple gear — the moment an Android phone, a Windows laptop, or a Linux box joins the room, it goes quiet. BIShare is the AirDrop alternative that works across iPhone, Android, Windows, Mac, and Linux: send files directly when you share a Wi-Fi network, or hand over a link the other person opens in any browser. Free, no account, no lock-in.

why.title: Why you might want an AirDrop alternative
why.body: AirDrop feels effortless — as long as everyone’s on Apple. It runs on Apple-only protocols, so it simply can’t reach an Android phone, a Windows PC, or a Linux machine. Google’s Quick Share and Microsoft’s Phone Link each patch part of the gap, but every one of them leaves someone out. BIShare takes the opposite bet: one tool that connects every platform, either directly over your network or through a plain browser link.

0.b: When both devices share a Wi-Fi network, files go straight from one to the other, end-to-end encrypted, never touching a server. No internet around? A phone hotspot works just as well.

1.b: You get a link, a QR code, and a 6-character code. The other person opens the link in any browser — Safari, Chrome, anything — and downloads. No app, no sign-up, and the link expires after 24 hours.

2.b: iPhone, Android, Windows, Mac, and Linux run the same BIShare. Send from any of them to any of them — or to someone who only has a browser open.

rows.r1: Receive with just a browser link, no app
rows.r2: Works nearby and over the internet

0.q: What is the best AirDrop alternative?
0.a: For most people it’s BIShare, because it does what AirDrop does — instant, direct, encrypted transfers — but across iPhone, Android, Windows, Mac, and Linux instead of Apple devices only. It also adds a browser-link mode so you can send to someone who isn’t nearby, or who has no app at all.

1.q: Is there an AirDrop alternative that works between iPhone and Android?
1.a: Yes. AirDrop can’t reach Android at all, but BIShare handles iPhone ↔ Android in both directions. On the same Wi-Fi it transfers directly, device to device; apart, it gives you a link the other phone opens in its browser to download the file.

2.q: Is there a free AirDrop alternative with no account?
2.a: BIShare is free and needs no sign-up. Nearby transfers over your own network have no size caps, and share links work for anyone on any platform. Large files up to 100 GB go over a link for free, and that link auto-expires in 24 hours.

3.q: Is an AirDrop alternative as private and secure as AirDrop?
3.a: BIShare is built for it. Direct transfers are end-to-end encrypted and stay on your local network — nothing is stored on a server. That matters, because many older ‘share’ apps aren’t encrypted and route files through the cloud. BIShare doesn’t.

4.q: Can I use an AirDrop alternative without installing anything?
4.a: To receive, yes. When someone sends you a BIShare link, you just open it in any browser and download — no app, no account on your end. Installing the app only makes nearby transfers faster and unlocks every feature; it’s never required to receive.

cta.title: One app that reaches every device you own
cta.body: Free, no account. Install BIShare on your phone, laptop, or desktop and start sending — the other side doesn’t even need the app.
